title: Opening range breakout
hypothesis: The high and low of the first minutes of the session mark levels where a break tends to continue for the rest of the day, most strongly in leveraged index ETFs.

title: Liquidity sweep and fair value gap reversal
hypothesis: A push through a prior swing high or low that fails and leaves a three-bar price gap (fair value gap) marks trapped traders; price tends to reverse back through the gap.
data_needed: 1-minute OHLCV, regular hours. Prior-day and session swing levels are derived from the same bars.

title: Trend pullback to VWAP
hypothesis: On a trending day, the session VWAP acts as a mean that institutions defend; the first pullbacks to it are entries in the direction of the trend.
data_needed: 1-minute OHLCV, regular hours (VWAP is computed from bar volume)

title: Intraday momentum breakouts
hypothesis: A close through a recent N-bar high or low on above-average volume or range starts a move that continues long enough to trade.

title: Intraday mean reversion
hypothesis: Short-lived stretches away from an intraday mean (VWAP, a moving average, Bollinger bands) in liquid index ETFs snap back more often than they extend.

title: Intraday trend following
hypothesis: Once an intraday trend is established on 5- to 30-minute bars (moving-average or channel rules), it persists into the close often enough to pay for the false starts.
data_needed: 1-minute OHLCV, regular hours (higher timeframes are aggregated from it)

title: Pairs trading on daily bars
hypothesis: The spread between closely related ETFs (SPY/QQQ, SPY/IWM, SPY/DIA) mean-reverts; trade it long one leg and short the other when it stretches.
data_needed: Daily OHLCV for both legs. A broader universe of related stocks would give many more pairs.

title: Short-term mean reversion on daily bars
hypothesis: Index ETFs that close sharply down for a few days (low short-period RSI, close near the day's low) tend to bounce over the next few sessions.

title: Momentum breakouts on daily bars
hypothesis: A close at a new N-day high marks the start of a multi-week advance; exit on a shorter-period low.

title: Trend following on daily bars
hypothesis: Assets that have risen over the past months keep rising; hold what is above its long moving average and leave what is not.
data_needed: Daily OHLCV for the 8 ETFs is enough for a reduced form. The published strategy needs a broad multi-asset universe (commodity, currency, rate and equity-index futures), which the catalog does not have: file that as a non-blocking data request.
